# dsh-rea

A DeepSeek Harness plugin bundle
that mounts the **REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)** MCP server as t

he `rea` tool
namespace — and gives it an ordinary on/off switch in the **Plugins** page.

This package ships **no analysis engine, no tool implementation, and no model
code**. It is a declar

ation: one MCP bridge row, plus the display metadata that
makes it a card in the plugin list. Every

actual REA tool is discovered from the
`rea-agents` package at run time.
## Why a bundle instead of a YAML snippet

Dropping the same six lines into `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.yml` works, but that row is
invisible to the P

lugins page — the page lists **bundles** (packages that carry a
`dsh.bundle.patch`), not free-standi

ng rows. Wrapping the row in a bundle is what
turns it into a switch you can click, or click back of
f after the investigation.

The switch matters because the `rea` namespace is expensive while it is on: about
200 tool schemas t
ravel in **every** request.
| State | Tools sent | Tool-definition context |

| dsh-rea off | ~40 built-in | ~2K–8K tokens |
| dsh-rea on | ~40 + ~207 | **~200K tokens** |

Measured against `rea-agents@6.5.0` on a 1M-token window: the schemas serialize to
~790 KB, which th

e harness prices at ~207K tokens, roughly 20% of the window. The
figure moves with the REA release;
it is never zero while the bundle is on.
## Install
From GitHub:

Or from a local checkout, which is the form to use while developing this package:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Installation also **selects** the bundle, so `rea` tools appear right away; switch it
off in the Plu

gins page when you are done. Grab the
matching skill from `rea-agents` (or from the REA repository)

if you want the
model to have REA's own procedure guidance; this package deliberately does not
dupli

ant the
model to have REA's own procedure guidance; this package deliberately does not
duplicate it.

The REA server itself is not downloaded at install time. The bridge runs
`npx -y rea-agents@latest m

cp`, so npm fetches the newest release on the first
tool sync after the switch is turned on (and reu
ses its cache afterwards).
## Turn it off and on
**Plugins page → Installed plugins → dsh-rea** — flip the switch.

- **On** — the MCP bridge starts, lists REA's tools, and registers them under
`mcp__rea__*`.
- **Off

** — the row is withdrawn, the child process is disposed, and the tool
schemas stop being sent. Late
r requests are ~200K tokens lighter.

The switch is a profile-level setting: it applies to every session of the profile,
including session

s that are already open. Turning it off while a REA call is
running cancels that call.

No restart is needed when HMR is enabled (the default in Desktop and Web
profiles). Without HMR, the
change applies on the next start.
## Configuration

Defaults live in `cordis.patch.yml`. Override the `rea-mcp`
row from your profile patch when you nee

d to pin a REA version, raise the call
timeout for slow decompilation, or make startup failures loud

to pin a REA version, raise the call
timeout for slow decompilation, or make startup failures loud:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A patch **replaces** a row's whole `config` rather than merging into it, so restate
every key you wa

eplaces** a row's whole `config` rather than merging into it, so restate
every key you want to keep.
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `serverName` | `rea` | Namespace of the tool names (`mcp__rea__<tool>`); max 32 chars |
| `command

` / `args` | `npx` + `-y rea-agents@latest mcp` | The stdio server to launch |
| `toolCallTimeoutMs`

| `60000` | Per-call budget; raise it for long analyses |
| `failOnStartupError` | `false` | `true`

fails the plugin instead of silently exposing no tools |
| `reconnect` | built-in policy | Retry/ba
ckoff when the child process drops |
## Verify what it costs

The context meter above the composer breaks usage into system prompt, tool
definitions, and messages

. Toggle the bundle and compare the **tool definitions**
row — that delta is what this plugin costs.

Alternatively, read the latest
`request/header` from a session log under `~/.dsh/sessions/` and cou

nt the
`mcp__rea__*` entries.
## Uninstall

Plugins page → dsh-rea → **Remove**. Removing the bundle unregisters the row and
lets you delete the

package; the `npx` cache is outside the profile and stays
until npm or `npx` clears it.
